Then again, I'm not exactly one to talk – I still have a ways to go before I can paint like Zaza. And I don't even know if that day will ever come, considering how much I like skipping school. Especially when it means I can watch the Exalts in action!

NAME: Mountain Nymph
FLAVOR_TEXT: From a mere pebble, she creates a sparkling jewel.
INSPIRATION: The Oreads are mountain and cave nymphs. The most famous are Echo, who fell in love with Narcissus; Sinoe, a wet nurse of Pan; Oenone, the first wife of Paris; and Chelone, who was transformed into a tortoise by Hermes. They are sisters of the Curetes and the Satyrs, and are part of Artemis' entourage. As such, they are huntresses in addition to their role as the guardian divinities of mountains.
STORY:
393 AC - I'm late, and I'm going to catch a scolding if I don't hurry. Not only from Zaza, but from Mom and Dad as well. I know it was hard to accept the Matriarch's decision and to let me go off alone onto dry land. But Bubbles and I are an Exalt now. I still can't believe it, actually. From afar, we had all watched the exploration forces depart. We'd watched the Solstice Gate open, Kojo and the Kraken, the liberation of Kuraokami… So when the Clan had received the call, it had come as a complete shock. And when the Matriarch summoned me to her office when we arrived, it had been even more of a shock.

But thinking about that now won't get me where I'm going any quicker. If I'm not at the meeting point soon, there'll be hell to pay. I need to charge down the mountain at full throttle, as Kojo puts it, and the best way to get to the bottom is obviously a landslide. I call on an Oread, because those nymphs are the perfect choice in this situation. Besides, the rule was clear: As long as I didn't have complete control over my Alteration, I needed to at least be supervised by an Eidolon. With my paintbrush, I paint rocks in a style inspired by August Macke. With help from the nymph, I can control the landslip and surf the rocks. But maybe I should also paint myself a helmet, because you never know what might happen…

NAME: Forest Nymph
FLAVOR_TEXT: From an innocent seed, she creates wild forests.
INSPIRATION: There are two types of tree and forest nymphs: the dryads and the hamadryads. Dryads are connected to forested areas as a whole, whereas hamadryads are bonded to a single tree and share the same fate: They die if the tree dies or is cut down. Karya for the walnut tree, Sykea for the fig, Morea for the mulberry, Balanos for the oak… There are eight hamadryads in all, and each looks after a specific type of tree.
STORY:
393 AC - Zaza always says that Art never imitates reality, but instead gives it meaning. Because when it comes down to it, there is no meaning in reality. What exists exists, and that's all there is to it. But an Alterer's job is to do the complete opposite. It's to create meaning and to manifest it in the world. For the Lyra, the Tumult has always been a sort of breeding ground, with all sorts of ideas floating around. Literally. We harvest them like fruit, and we create with them, like a painter with their pigments. They must first be combined, and then you daub them over reality, using Mana as a fixative. Dad often says that times have changed – that reality no longer precedes Art, and that it's almost the opposite now.

Zaza really stumped me last time. She asked me what we were. Humans, Eidolons, Chimaeras… Which came first? Like the chicken and the egg. But she gave me a clue. If a Chimaera could keep its form based on how others perceived it, and if Eidolons could change based on each person's imagination, was it not also the same for beings in the real world? I look over at the dryad, which had sat down in the hollow of a tree while I collected dead wood for a fire. I manifest some leaves of gouache to flutter around her, to thank her for guiding me through the forest. At the end of the day, am I more real than her?

NAME: Lyra Aerialist
FLAVOR_TEXT: The Cloth Dancers' great talent is to use every rough spot to adapt to their environment.
STORY:
393 AC - I watch them descend from the heights as I collect a little water from the waterfall, and while Bubbles takes a dip between the rocks. They unfurl their colorful ribbons and fall, perfectly at ease in the air. I had seen Clan Kasirga aerialists before at a previous Kalann Mae, in the Makonis Heights after the circus big top had been put up. Their acrobats and trapeze artists had put on their show to the sound of dramatic drum rolls before our clowns took over with their silly antics. It was one of the rare moments when the Lyra Clans came together, and those special times never lasted more than a few days. And each time it was a celebration.

That's why it still felt a bit strange to be able to spend so much time with them. The Ouroboros and Wayfarer traveled side by side, and there were frequent shuttles between the two Sahankas. Well, I still wasn't allowed to visit the Kasirga casinos, but Mom had already taken me to the circus twice. But the best thing was the pajama parties and sleepovers with the other kids. We told each other stories, even if it meant getting to sleep late, and we also taught each other different skills. "I'll show you how to walk on a slackline if you teach me how to juggle…" That kind of thing. But the real novelty was being with kids from other Factions, and even some who weren't part of any Faction…

NAME: Nuit
FLAVOR_TEXT: Gone is the sun, and again comes the night.
INSPIRATION: Nuit is a goddess from Egyptian mythology. She is the personification of the sky and heavens, as well as all celestial phenomena. Mother of the stars and protector of the earth, she also gave birth to Osiris, Seth, Isis and Nephthys by mating with her twin brother Geb, who represents the earth. Every evening, it's said that Nuit makes the sun disappear within her, then makes it reappear in the morning, thus illustrating her nocturnal journey across the sky.
STORY:
393 AC - With the tips of my fingers, I flick the hairs of my brush to splatter white dots on my canvas, making stars. Then I wipe my hand on my apron and take a few steps back to admire my work. Dad always says you need to stand back to properly look at what you've done. When you're too close, you focus too much on the details. You notice all the faults, all the inaccuracies… But what's important is the overall view. It's Nuit, hugging the sun. She cradles it, and will soon cover it with her cloak of stars and darkness to bring on the night. I love to paint. I've known that since I was very little. It's probably why I have such a visual imagination.

I look at the painting from every angle. If I want to summon Nuit and make night fall, I need to remember every detail of the scene: the constellations, the starlight, the moons… was I right to paint three of them? I shrug. If I want to make her more real, it's easier if all viewers can clearly understand who she is. OK, note for later: Add golden patterns that recall Egyptian gods… And why not show an eclipse happening? Rather pleased with myself, I go to the sink to clean my brushes with thinner. And on the way, I tell Bubbles not to swim too close to my daubing.

NAME: Koi, Playful Leviathan
FLAVOR_TEXT: Its gracious leap parted the clouds, revealing our path forward.
STORY:
393 AC - Its multicolored silhouette is reflected in the stagnant water of the rice fields, which are full to brimming after the recent rains. I watch intently to ensure I don't miss a single moment of the show. And what a show it is! Its pastel-colored fins push the clouds away each time they flap, like the rippling, lacy fins of a betta fighting fish. As it twists in the sky, like the fish-shaped streamers often flown during Ryukkōsai, its whiskers stir the air around it like those of a catfish. But there's really no mistaking it: This mischievous Leviathan specifically chose to be a carp as big as a mountain to announce its existence in the world. Its iridescent scales reflect the sunlight and start to shimmer.

It looks like it's dancing, or engaging in a courtship ritual. But I know it's actually playing with my alter ego. I can also see the sparkling droplets that Bubbles forms as he swims around the Leviathan, and the giant Koi happily follows him, curious and playful. After all, Chimaeras and Leviathans aren't that different, really. I don't know yet if other humans realize how closely related they were. They surely knew that both were connected to Mana and the Tumult, and could freely wade around in it as though it were an ordinary ocean. But did they understand their true nature and what their role was? I take out my notebook and charcoal and prepare to sketch the aerial ballet. I simply must show this to Zaza.

NAME: Eris
FLAVOR_TEXT: You win some, you lose some.
INSPIRATION: Eris is the goddess of discord in Greek mythology. She is the daughter of Nyx and the sister of Ares, the god of war. She is also the mother of many nasty children: Ponos (Toil), Lethe (Oblivion), Limos (Hunger), Phonoi and Machai (Murders and Battles), Dysnomia and Ate (Anarchy and Ruin), Algea (Pains), Hysminai (Fights), Androktasiai (Slayings), Neikea (Quarrels), Amphillogiai (Disputes), Pseudea (Lies) and Horkos (Oath).
STORY:
393 AC - Total respect. The look. The attitude. The power. I love it. Goddesses – they totally rock! When you're deep in a… sorry… at the top of a flying island where there's nothing but a constant stream of falling water (which ruins all my spray paints… great!), let's just say a goddess showing up can really save the day. I tried to repaint everything and make it nicer, but it doesn't work too well with all the rain. We were SOOOOO bored. So I thought it was a good time for a bit of gambling, just to get everyone to relax a little. At first, the others laughed when I suggested a game of dice. But when I pulled out the money, suddenly they were all interested. I laid down my terms: Bring a partner. They said OK. Pfff, what idiots.

Eris appeared, her wings beating in the wind, and landed on our rock with her charming smile. And without further ado, the betting started. The dice rolled, money changed hands. The pot grew. Those cheeky devils were hiding notes in their socks. Ha! And they talk about the smell of money! It certainly does smell when it's hidden next to your feet. A little wink between friends. And that, ladies and gentlemen, is when all hell broke loose. She won it all in just a few throws. She left them with nothing but their socks (well, not literally). And then they starting yelling at each other. There was almost a big brawl. I was laughing so much my sides ached. It'd been a long time since I'd laughed so much on an expedition. Not only that, we shared the winnings… 50% for me and 50% for… the genius who came up with the idea.

NAME: Daikokuten
FLAVOR_TEXT: If you never take a risk, you'll never be rewarded.
INSPIRATION: Daikokuten is the Japanese deity of commerce, trade and wealth. He is depicted as a smiling man with a rotund belly, surrounded by sacks of rice (symbol of happiness). Over his shoulder is a large sack containing wisdom and patience. In his right hand he carries a wooden mallet (uchide no kozuchi), a symbol of the virtue of work.
STORY:
393 AC - It's nice to have earned a load of cash from the sweat of your brow. What's that? Dishonestly? First of all, how dare you! And secondly, deception requires a great deal of effort and creativity. But seriously, you think I just sit there twiddling my thumbs? Yes, I'm talking to you. And tell the rest of the peanut gallery to keep their comments to themselves, OK? Now that I have your attention, it's important to know that theft on its own is never good enough. You need to know how to capitalize on it. You need to know how to double down. And that's why… I take an Effigy of Daikokuten out of my bag, and place it on the little island. And you know what? Stealing it out from under the nose – and very long beard – of that damned Afanas was no mean feat.

The divinity materializes when I smash the statuette, and he's brought all his gear with him: sack, mallet and bales of rice. If there's one god that can congratulate me on my ingenuity, it's him. In a corridor once, I overheard some Ordis scholars talking about him and certain traditions involving him, which I found particularly interesting. It's called fukunusubi, or "theft of fortune", where you steal an idol from a temple without getting caught, then sell it to the highest bidder. Obviously that's the kind of guy I like, because he gets how these things work: nothing ventured, nothing gained. So cough it up, because I followed the instructions to the letter!

NAME: Lost in the Riptide
FLAVOR_TEXT: This is why you're supposed to read the map...
STORY:
393 AC - I grab Bubbles' fin to let him pull me along, because there's not a single second to waste. On the ledge, the three Eidolons already need to hold on tight to avoid being swept away by the surge. Zaza and I had warned everyone that this place was dangerous! At regular intervals, gravity currents would grab hold of the water that had accumulated on the archipelagos to form the huge water spheres of the Thermaic Quadrant. But it seemed like not everyone had listened, or even read the map! Even way up here, I can see the Three Little Pigs fighting as hard as they can to avoid getting sucked in. They've discarded their bags, packs and cumbersome gear, but it doesn't seem to be enough…

Deep down, I know they're just Eidolons and don't really fear anything – except remembering a really bad experience and having it become a habit for them. But we're an Exalt now, and that changes everything. We need to act like heroes! What would Sigismar and Wingspan do? Or Kojo and Booda? They were my favorite duos. That's the question I asked myself before jumping in, and the answer was obvious: They would have jumped in without hesitation. That's why I needed to do the same, even if it meant I'd get a proper scolding later. After all, with great power comes great responsibility!

NAME: Lyra Signet
FLAVOR_TEXT: Creation and transformation.

NAME: The Western Wind
FLAVOR_TEXT: It's no use going against the Wind.
INSPIRATION: In Greek mythology, Zephyr is the god of the west wind. He represents a warm, light and favorable wind that can delay or increase harvests. Son of the Titans Astreaus and Eos, he is one of the eight directional winds, the Anemoi, which also includes Eurus, Kaikias, Notus, Apeliotes, Lips, Boreas and Skiron.
STORY:
393 AC - I grumble as I watch the blue swan disappear over the horizon, clearly ahead of schedule, and I wonder if it really is the bearer of Zephyr – the wind, of course, just to be clear. Judging by its name, it must be. But whether that's enough proof… Ha! Speaking of weather, I'm going to need a whole bag of it. The one Aeolus gave to Odysseus, to be precise. Hey, Fen, a little help here, please! If anyone can whisper a few sweet words to the Wind, it's you, sweetheart! I yell to the merry band of laggards to hold on tight to their umbrellas as the wind begins to turn, gently at first, to a light, warm breeze. Then the gusts blow stronger, and in a clear direction. Watch out, folks, this might be a bumpy ride… so hold on tight!

The startled faces of my companions switch from puzzlement to worry when I make a colorful umbrella appear in everyone's hand. The sudden gust of wind propels us forward like a pile of dead leaves in autumn, while my other half scrambles for cover. I discard my outfit to unfurl my wings, which are obviously better suited to the situation than a heavy leather jacket. Go on, blow stronger! Even stronger! We've got a bird to catch, dammit! We just have to ride the breeze, at least until the wind turns, like a nanny floating down between cherry trees. Especially since, for a fraction of a second there, I felt something staring at me from beneath the clouds…

NAME: Mapmaker's Boon
FLAVOR_TEXT: Each of us paints their own reality.
STORY:
393 AC - I remember the first time I stepped into Zaza's workshop. It was completely different from the Painthouse with its big bay windows. Hers was dark, and a complete mess as well. Painting had always been my escape, especially when the other children teased me. They gave me a hard time because I didn't talk much. But what they didn't understand was that my language was pictures, not words. And when I started to paint the world, the Matriarch put me in Zahira's care, because she was a mapmaker and she painted the world in her own way. At first, I didn't think it was the same at all. For me, drawing a map wasn't the same thing as drawing from real life. But over time, I began to see that it wasn't all that different after all.

At first, I just made whatever I felt like. I painted using my instincts and picked whatever subject grabbed me. But Zahira would always tell me that I needed to start with the basics. Reproduce, imitate, copy. She told me that was the best way to improve my technique, and that style would come later. It was good advice, sure, but it was boring! I had to be more accurate, always more accurate. But after a while, I noticed that when I painted the outside world, I was better at identifying what I wanted to do and expressing what was in my head. When I told her about it, Zaza called it "mastering your imagination". And even Bubbles' traits had become more refined as a result. I think it was all designed to prepare us for becoming an Exalt ourselves.

NAME: The Painthouse
FLAVOR_TEXT: The paints of the Tisdhera still perfume the heights of the Wayfarer.
STORY:
393 AC - Bubbles floats under the glass roof, and it looks like his fins are caressing the sky. It's like we're in an aquarium. Everyone says he's my Chimaera, but Bubbles is much more than that. He's my confidant, my friend, my reflection. He's the one I talk to about getting bullied at school. He's the one I hold in my arms when I have something on my mind. And that'll never change. I look at the statue that my father recently sculpted. And I know he'll frown when he sees that my fishy-fish has been rubbing up against it. But I also know that he's used to the mess we make. He'll sigh, maybe scold Bubbles a bit, and then that will be that. All right, just a few more brush strokes. I need to finish my painting.

The sky. The clouds. The flying islands. I add movement to my painting to make it look more alive. I went through my ukiyo-e phase, and then my impressionist phase. Fauvism is what interests me now, although Art Nouveau and Klimt are increasingly catching my eye. It would be cool to paint portraits of Exalts now that we're going to be part of the group. That's what the Matriarch told us when we arrived at the City of Scholars. I suddenly notice that the sky has gone dark above us, and I make some garlands bloom over our heads. I wonder where Dad and Mom are, then remember that they've gone off to help the circus by putting makeup on the clowns, pierrots and harlequins. Cool, that means Bubbles and I will get some alone time.

NAME: The Opera House
FLAVOR_TEXT: The Arkaster Opera House is known as the Spark, for that's where stars are born.
STORY:
393 AC - Nostalgia is a double-edged sword. It brings both comfort and torture. I was still young when I first performed at The Spark. I could have become a diva. The one and only. I could have captivated the crowds, enchanted entire audiences. But fate had other ideas for me, and took me under – or should I say "over" – foreign skies. As I see it open out before, I think of a jewelry box. One with a diamond in the middle, either rough and uncut or at the peak of its art and brilliance. The Spark can look like whatever you want it to look like, and this evening it will be all gold and silk. There will be ribbons for the aisles, and French-style platforms for the balconies. And the stage…

The stage will be a rocky precipice, with a "Wanderer Above the Sea of Fog" vibe. Dramatic and epic. Rrrr. Everything I love. On top will be a glorious frame, poetic even, wrapped in violet ribbons, like a gift box waiting to be opened… And the gift? Me, of course, in one of my most beautiful costumes. I'll appear in a shower of fireworks, and everyone will chant my name. I open my eyes and slip out of my daydream. I'll always be a diva. But now my other duties prevent me from being the celebrity I could have been. Should I regret it? With a smile, I let my fantasies dissolve like snow melting in the sun. There's no comfort for me behind the mask of nostalgia. Just the torture of what will never be.

NAME: Kauri & Puff
FLAVOR_TEXT: The language of nature has no use for words

NAME: Resentful Robin
FLAVOR_TEXT: Despite their small size, Rhodopean robins will defend their territory with beak and claw.
STORY:
393 AC - I sneak a peek at the sky from my shelter, looking for any trace of dark clouds. I poke my head between the branches and pull myself up out of the bush. But the sky is clear. There's no sign of the wyvern on the horizon. I go back down to Puff, who is tending to his wounds. His downy wool is stained with red, and I clench my teeth. Maybe with my help… I focus and feel the Mana around me. I know I shouldn't take too much, but if I could just use a tiny little bit, maybe it will help Puff to heal… The leaves of the shrub shrivel as I breathe in the energy that keeps them alive, then blow it towards the Chimaera.

Just then, I hear a shrill twittering coming out of the bare branches. A robin with green, yellow and white wings flits towards the ram to give him an earful, then tries to peck at him while beating its wings furiously. I step in and try to chase it away by waving my arms around. Puff needs rest after his fight, and deserves to be left alone. That's when I notice the nest of twigs, which was previously hidden but is now uncovered. The bird beats its wings and gives me a couple of pecks between shrieks. And you know what? I deserve it. Its clutch of eggs is now in danger from predators, and it's all my fault.

NAME: Helpful Pelican
FLAVOR_TEXT: It's not unusual to see these pelicans ferrying small local creatures from one island to the next.
STORY:
393 AC - The constantly shifting nature of the flying islands means that these ecosystems are in a perpetual state of transition. When a suspended fragment drifts, its exposure to the sun changes, which causes increased evaporation of its bodies of water, sometimes resulting in drought… And I'm currently in one of those dried-up rivers. The stones in the riverbed are even starting to show, and the few puddles that remain here and there will be nothing but memories soon. For the fish that have managed to find refuge, it's only a matter of time before they perish. I hear the beating of wings. I turn to see an enormous pelican land near a pond. For a brief moment, I wonder if it's one of the ones that accompanies Nanshe when she visits the orphans… But no, it's only interested in the pool and what's floundering within it.

Fry are certainly easy prey in these conditions. But instead of pecking at them and gobbling them up, the bird opens its beak and slowly immerses it, just enough so that its pouch fills with water. Then the fish and fry dart into it, as though it were a swimming pool. Ah, of course! If the fish disappeared from the islands, it would be bad news for the birds that live here and depend on them for their survival. When nature is cruel, cooperation is essential. It's only in a world of plenty that competition can thrive. It's a fundamental law of nature. The pelican suddenly flies off, transporting its little passengers. It will probably release them in another pond, lake or stream. So that life can continue.

NAME: Eru, Emissary of the Wild
FLAVOR_TEXT: "Surrounded by all of his animal friends, my teacher never felt alone, even living as a hermit." - Kauri
STORY:
393 AC - Papa is on one side of the fire, and Mama is on the other, with the light of the flames dancing on their faces. They are wearing their ceremonial clothes and ritual face paint. As for Eru, he's standing next to me with a reassuring hand on my shoulder. He squeezes it one last time, then lets go so I can move forward to the young Ollam and the dark figure of Puff, who are both waiting for me on the other side of the flames. We're not alone, of course. Many animals answered my mentor's call to be witnesses to our union. Raccoons, anteaters, common cranes, turtles and tarantulas… A wolf watches from the edge of the clearing, its eyes glinting in the half-light.

"Are you sure about this?" my father asked me. I'd replied yes, but to be honest, I didn't really know what I was getting myself into. I just felt like it was the right path to follow. The Musubi came from the Skein. From what I understood, it was like stitching two people together with threads of Mana. Described like that, I admit it didn't sound like much fun. I'd heard two grown-ups at the Mess talking about the difference between the Skein and the Ordis Gestalt. From what they were saying, it was a bit like the difference between the soul and the spirit, although I don't really know what that means… Ow! Eru taps me on the head to bring me back from my daydreaming. He knows I often drift off, like when I'm sprawled in the grass, supposedly guarding the Woollybacks…

NAME: Armored Bird
FLAVOR_TEXT: He raised a shield of feathers. Lances and harpoons shattered against his steely wings.
STORY:
393 AC - At first, I thought of Alteration like a necklace with pearls threaded onto it one by one – amber, jade, and so on. Each of them is an idea. And when the necklace is finished, all the pearls form a whole. But Eru told me that was just one of a thousand ways of thinking about it, and so there were many more. The way I was taught, in the traditional Muna fashion, was more like a tapestry, in which the threads create shapes, and those shapes represent things. We weave and we unravel. It's like a patchwork. But that's not totally accurate, because the Skein is a mesh. When I embroider, the Skein brings me ideas from everything around me.

That's why the "jade" comes from a hunter, who used to watch his grandfather make jewelry in the back room of his shop; and the stylized bird comes from the logo of an Axiom airship, which a young pilot took the time to paint with love and care just under the cockpit, as a lucky charm… All of that filters through the Skein to the tapestry I'm stitching, the entity I'm in the middle of manifesting. Something strong enough to withstand the hunters' explosive spears – gulp! – but quick enough to catch up to Soledad and avoid Halua's fins. One last cross stitch and… there, just in time. I turn towards the hunters, who swoop down from the sky like birds of prey.

NAME: Colorful Cuckoo
FLAVOR_TEXT: Even the shyest become a bit less reserved when they hear its song.
STORY:
393 AC - As I watch the cuckoo's egg crack and hatch, I think to myself how it's a bit like what happened to Papa. I was dumped on his doorstep one day, totally out of the blue. If he'd had other children, I would have monopolized his attention to the detriment of my hypothetical brothers and sisters. Although I don't think I would have gone as far as kicking them out of the house. But who knows… Hypothetically, they could have been so unbearable to live with that I had no other choice! Anyway… That's not what I'm here for. The egg breaks, and a beak emerges uncertainly from the shell. I came here to categorize the endemic species of the various Quadrants, and I had my work cut out for me!

When you look at the archipelago's islands, you can see a similar phenomenon across all the ecosystems: a slow succession of species. One would replace another, like a giant game of musical chairs. But the process was happening much faster here than in the Katkera, probably because of the drifting atolls and the Tumult tides, which were having a major impact on the living conditions on the surface of the islands… The pieces of broken shell fall away, and a head pushes through the gap. The chick doesn't yet have the colorful plumage of the adult cuckoos, just a few grayish feathers to help it blend into its environment. Suddenly, the sky darkens. I look up, puzzled. It's as if the clouds had changed color. As if something had blocked the sun's rays…

NAME: Migratory Crane
FLAVOR_TEXT: When the cranes start their migration, that's the signal that it's time to seek out new horizons.
STORY:
393 AC - I watch the cranes extend their wings, while the fish that Orchid just caught sizzles on the flat stone I had placed in the fire. They rise gracefully, and I hear the splashing of water followed by the beating of feathers. Nature always sends signals. They're barely noticeable to many of us: a slight change in temperature, a wind picking up from a specific direction, the sky darkening in a unique way when the sun disappears at a certain point behind a certain mountain… It's the signal to leave, to move to another place. All too often, we forget that we are "programmed" by nature, as Treyst likes to put it. But our senses and subconscious never forget. Our unbreakable link with nature is encoded in our instincts.

And so I wonder… I wonder to what extent the Expeditionary Corps, and the entire Rediscovery Endeavor for that matter, are really the result of a choice, rather than a necessity we feel deep within us. Maybe there are actually thousands of signals all around us, telling us that the time has come, that it's time to leave… I watch the cranes soaring in the sky. Their silhouettes stand out against the brooding gray of the clouds. It's believed that they can sense magnetic waves and energy lines, and that they know where they're going when they migrate. I wish I could say the same. Orchid told me that none of the places we had been were like the place where she had found me. So we have no choice but to keep moving…

NAME: Drowsy Dodo
FLAVOR_TEXT: After all that work, it's time for the dodo to go night-night.
INSPIRATION: The dodo from Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is, according to Lewis Carroll himself, a caricature of the author, whose real name was Charles Lutwidge Dodgson. Suffering from a stutter in his childhood, when creating the dodo character, the writer remembered the many times he tried to pronounce his name but only managed "Do-do-dodgson" instead. In the book, the dodo organizes a race with strange and useless rules, which the author undoubtedly intended as a satire of the Victorian society he was living in.
STORY:
393 AC - I haul myself onto the secluded islet, then stretch my back, which is all sore after climbing this series of islands. Each time I try to contact Spike, all I get back in return are some fleeting and sometimes incoherent feelings. He's just over there on the next rock, probably in the middle of… I raise an eyebrow. A large ball of colorful feathers is nodding its head, while a large bubble of sleep emerges from the hole in its beak. It's almost comical, really. He's barely staying upright, leaning on his cane as if it's the twisted mast of a rudderless ship. O…kay… And, of course, I see Spike wrapped up in the bird's plumage as if it were a quilted blanket.

It seems both of them are having a siesta. In his half-sleep, the Eidolon recites a string of cryptic words in a croaky voice… "If both player’s markers meet at the same time, first check if any player moved forward further than necessary to win the game. If one player did and the other did not, the player who did wins the game. Otherwise, players play a tiebreaker Day in the Arena. The Arena is on the back of the Companion region card. Place it in the center of the table and put both players' Expedition markers on it." I place a hand on Spike's head. I don't know what arena you're talking about, but you won't win the race if you're asleep…

NAME: Wyvern
FLAVOR_TEXT: With their fluffy texture and cotton-candy flavor, woollybacks are wyverns' favorite prey.
INSPIRATION: A wyvern, also known as a guivre in heraldry, is a magical mythical creature from European folklore. It is depicted as a bipedal dragon, or sometimes as a winged serpent. Wyverns often guard treasure or block the way for knights errant.
STORY:
393 AC - An ominous crackling, then a deafening boom… The sound of the lightning is even more terrifying than usual. Where are my Woollybacks? I run to the ridge as the clouds rumble. There they are, soaked and trembling, huddled together at the top of a tiny hill. It's going to be tricky to get them down from there… I look up at the sky and gulp. Since the transhumance started, the weather has never gotten this bad this quickly before. I need to find shelter for them, and fast. Puff is bleating non-stop, urging the other sheep to get moving and follow him. I wipe away the rain trickling down my face and look for somewhere to shelter…

Crack. Boom. I see it appear in the bright flash of the lightning, like a bird of prey. It's huge, with enormous wings I can almost see through, and its back bristles with protruding spikes. And then it starts to swoop down towards my little woolly friends! I sprint towards them to tell them to run, but with the wind, rain and chaos, they don't hear me. Suddenly, Puff leaps in, swinging his horns from right to left. He moves as if to charge and stares at the dragon defiantly, without fear. The rain lashes down around us, and I need to squint to see what's going on. In a moment of clarity, I suddenly understand. I realize he's buying time so I can lead the flock to the sheep-pen.

NAME: Zaratan, Social Leviathan
FLAVOR_TEXT: We were sailing among the islands when one of them came to meet us.
STORY:
393 AC - I stand before him in my ceremonial robes. Sig insisted that I be accompanied by bodyguards from the Tagmata, but I know that a few soldiers won't make much difference if the Leviathan decides to get aggressive. No, all I can feel in the Skein is a combination of curiosity and joy. If he smashed our ship, it would be out of playfulness or clumsiness. The result would still be the same, of course. His giant head draws closer to us. Our whole ship could fit into one of his nostrils, without even touching the sides. We're nothing but ants compared to him. But the closer he comes, the more the dendrites of his Skein start groping around.

I feel his filaments tangling with mine, and he doesn't hold back, to say the least. In exchange, I ask for his hospitality. I share with him the key concepts of who we are – not through intellect, but more in relation to our underlying nature, the good and the bad… even though these concepts are essentially very human. The gargantuan turtle asks me if we come from below, from under the clouds, and I reply that no, we come from much further away. Narrowing his eye, which looks like a tiny moon, he tells me that we look like those who came to see him before the archipelago broke up and dispersed. Before the red wing made them abandon these shores…

NAME: Kauri's Intervention
FLAVOR_TEXT: "This senseless hunt must stop!"
STORY:
393 AC - Why? The little human stands on her bird-thing, making a shield to protect me. Even worse, she has her back to me. I could just open my mouth and simply swallow her up. So, why? Why defend me like this and take my side when all I want is to destroy them? Emerald-colored waves swirl around her, transforming all the projectiles that the hunters can throw into flowered branches and boxwood thickets. And I remember. I remember Bronté. Her cloudy hair, just like her sister's. They would climb on my back, desperate for me to give them a ride. But that was before the end of the Fallow Period, before the biostimulants…

The young woman she had become stepped forward. She had a gentle smile, the same as when she was young and wanted to climb on my back. My instincts told me something wasn't right. Her sister was tense. There were guards all around. Bronté placed a hand on my head, right between my eyes. "You must stop interfering," she said. Stop? But that was my role… Without warning, the serrated harpoons, attached to heavy chains, had pierced my wings. I start to growl just thinking about the betrayal. The human had deceived me. She was traitorous and treacherous. She was greedy and destructive. Another ruse. Another betrayal. There's a sudden shock, and a voice echoes in my head. Wait.

NAME: Pan
FLAVOR_TEXT: He's definitely the black sheep around here!
INSPIRATION: Pan, whose father is Hermes and whose mother is a daughter of Dryops, is a capricious nature deity in Greek mythology. The god of shepherds and flocks is often depicted as a man with a bearded face and the hindquarters and hooves of a goat, like the satyrs he is often associated with. It is said that seeing him with his true appearance in your dreams is a sign of happiness.
STORY:
393 AC - As I stretch and rub my sleepy eyes, I realize my mouth is watering. Papa is cooking fried eggs on the cast-iron skillet – and maybe a few slices of bacon, based on that yummy smell. I yawn, blink and look around me. All the Woollybacks have wandered off onto the grassy plain. Most of them are grazing, but a few are having a nap, like us. But if Papa and I are both here, who's looking after… I see him playing around among the animals, causing more chaos than anything else. I watch him playing leapfrog, and my father bursts out laughing when Puff scratches the ground with his hooves.

The panicking Woollybacks start to run in all directions as that rascal Pan continues to get up to mischief. There's something very funny about the way he moves around and gets up to his pranks, but I also feel the Chimaera's annoyance. Eru is there, again, and I realize that I'm dreaming again, half awake and half asleep. I need to pick a side: remain a simple shepherd boy, or become more by embracing the way of the animals? After all, the Musubi is an extension of the Skein, and the Skein is a path already laid out before us. Pan smiles at me, as if his goal from the very beginning was to spark something within me. And then I finally understand which path I must follow…

NAME: Tāne
FLAVOR_TEXT: Firmly rooted like a tree, yet free like the birds, he embodies nature's strength.
INSPIRATION: Tāne is a deity in Maori mythology, the god of forests and birds. He is the son of Rangi, the sky father, and Papa, the earth mother. When he separates his parents, he brings about the world of Light, which plucks their many children out from the shadows where they were living.
STORY:
393 AC - I grit my teeth. When will we learn? When will we learn from our mistakes? Everything was flattened, broken and shattered by the explosion. From what I heard, the Axiom and the Bravos had conducted an experiment near here. They overloaded an Aerolith fragment with vibrations to measure its explosive properties. The experiment had been successful, but as for its results… Even here, miles from ground zero, branches had been ripped off, natural shelters destroyed, nests sent crashing to the ground… I suddenly feel a wave of sadness wash over me upon seeing a pile of broken shells. Using Alteration to repair this biome would take weeks. But the good Oneiros could restore it to its original state instinctively, and much more organically… Feather and leaf. Egg and seed.

He starts to walk among the bent and bare tree trunks. His fingers caress the distressed trees. Where he brushes against them, his color seems to rub off onto the lifeless bark, then rise to the branches. It turns into leaves, a soft green at first before darkening. The grass shoots up in concentric waves around his feet, and when the ripples reach the trees, the branches flower as if experiencing a new spring. Then Tāne raises his arms in the air. I feel his call through the Skein. Flocks of birds begin to circle above our heads, then alight on the branches and among the new foliage. I bow to the Eidolon, who now has dozens of colorful birds perching on his arms.

NAME: Puff's Challenge
FLAVOR_TEXT: Wearing red might have been a mistake...
STORY:
393 AC - Hmm. I narrow my eyes as I watch the cloud of powder dissipate. The little one seems unharmed, but that doesn't excuse what the huntress did. I hate hunters. I detest hunters. I trample them underfoot. And this one needs to be taught a lesson. I fight my initial instinct… or maybe it's the child's yells, grating annoyingly in the back of my mind, which are stopping me from going too far. One sharp prod with my horn would be enough. The battering ram sends the first huntress flying. How do they do it again? Ah yes, a kick, a few well-aimed hooves would smash their equipment and destroy their little jet boards, which look more like the plank a pirate's prisoner would be forced to walk than something you'd want to ride on.

Run, kiddo. I'll deal with them. Take your chance while I distract them. You have more important things to do, and you know it. From the corner of my mind, I feel him agree with me. With a powerful blow, I smash one of the wretched poacher's toys to pieces. With a swift kick, I get rid of another of those pests. I feel like I'm a bowling ball knocking down pins. What's their word for that again? Strike? Hang on, where's the kid now? Hmm. Up there. I see Kauri rushing towards the lead hunter's jet board, as oblivious as a lamb to the slaughter. There's no time to lose. I should get this over and done with so I can join him. Now he's part of my, er… flock.

NAME: Muna Signet
FLAVOR_TEXT: Harmony and sharing.
STORY:
393 AC - There's an inherent contradiction among the Muna. We do our utmost to maintain the balance of nature, parity between the species – animals, plants, and others – so that everything can live in harmony. But isn't that just interventionism? If we were to follow the laws of nature to the letter, we should leave all species alone to live and die naturally. A few years ago, Arjun had told me to think more deeply about it. And it had been several days before I went back to find them. Proud of myself, I told them that it was all about our place in the world. Not doing anything was like not existing, but we did exist. And human beings were part of nature. It was a mistake to think that we were separate from or above nature.

In nature, there's always a sweet spot between cooperation and competition to guarantee a healthy environment. And we have the perfect tool to find that sweet spot: the Skein. Through it, we can almost hear nature, and all its desires and complaints. And we can help it thrive. In a way, it's like we've agreed to be its agents. But I've always wondered why it's only the Muna that received this gift, and not all human beings. The cicadas sing under the olive trees, and I lift my straw hat to wipe my forehead.  I pick one more juicy tomato, which Arjun would definitely have appreciated. Come to think of it, I think I dreamed about them last night…

NAME: Counting Sheep
FLAVOR_TEXT: The deepest sleep is woven from the wool of sweet dreams.
STORY:
393 AC - Some people say that the imaginary world and the dream world are the same thing. They say that when you sleep, all those things on the other side flow into our heads. Eru tole me that if this was true, maybe it meant that we were all basically connected to this vast ocean… and to each other as well. So would the Skein let me visit that boy I met yesterday, the one with the curly red hair? Or the one I interrupted while he was painting? Spending the day with Woollybacks is nice, but sometimes you feel a bit lonely. I just hope I don't drown them in a sea of wool, since that's all I see all day long…

I'm suddenly aware that I'm sleeping. Eru is next to me, putting a log on the fire. So this is a dream. Sparks rise up into the night sky. We're never truly alone. That's what I hear him say. I see my parents, I see a squirrel, a mole, a small monkey… and a shadow in the forest. Never alone. Puff hits the bark of a tree with his horns. Thunk. Never alone. He looks at me. I mustn't forget that what he looks like is not actually who he is. Thunk. He may look like a ram, but it's just an act. I smell fire and meat…

NAME: Joining Fates
FLAVOR_TEXT: "Be united in the Musubi."
STORY:
393 AC - I'm a bit scared. Soledad is on one side, and she seems lost in her thoughts, uncertain of what's to come. On the other side is the Leviathan, which could change its mind and eat us all up at any moment. And between those two, there's only me. A blacksmith would probably say between the hammer and anvil, but for me it's more like between the wolf and the edge of a cliff. Haha. I saw how the Ollam did it when Puff and I were being bound together. And thankfully, Puff is here to give me encouragement. "Hurry up, stop dragging your feet," he says. He's right. The more I hesitate, the greater the chance that all this will turn out badly. I take a deep breath, trying to remember what the high priest did during my Musubi.

I just need to do exactly the same thing, basically. It would be better with a design pattern. But I don't really know if there is one for this. It's a bit bigger and more complicated than a scarf… With my hands, I imitate what the Ollam did. He looked a little like an orchestra conductor (which I know because I recently saw one in real life for the very first time), but with a needle and thread instead of a baton. OK, I need to get going. Stitch two beings together. I'm suddenly aware of two young women looking at me, two Yzmir wizards watching what I'm doing in a slightly scary way. No, I can't get distracted…

NAME: Woolly Woolly Field
FLAVOR_TEXT: Talk about wild and woolly!
STORY:
393 AC - Yep, we'll definitely have our work cut out for us. The doors of the Ouroboros open, and the herd spills out into the pastures. When they're nose to tail like that, you can't tell where the clouds end and the field of wool begins… And then there's the near-deafening clanking of the bells. My father gestures to me, and I lift my crook to show that I've understood his instructions. I whistle to mark the start of the transhumance, and Puff grunts next to me to get the flock moving. The sea of white begins to roam the grassy slopes, chewing and bleating as they go. I look at the huge ram and scratch his neck.

We spent a lot of time together on the Lyra Sahanka. Every morning, I would fetch the hay and fill the bowls with grain. Although he was distrustful at first, the Chimaera would relax when I was around. Maybe because it was obvious to him that he didn't need to fear me. Of course, I was careful to treat the animals well, to calm them down when they felt too squeezed in or started to run amok. I was curious to know why he had taken on this form, why he had become their protector. But it's not as though we could really understand each other, except through the emotions that filter through the Skein…

NAME: Woollyback
FLAVOR_TEXT: The warmth of wool and the softness of cotton candy, now together on four legs.
STORY:
393 AC - A few whistles and loud clacks with the tongue are enough. I hear the bells before I see them appear over the ridge and come running down the hill. I make a few more clicking sounds, then a whoop to guide the Woollybacks, which file past in front of me and flock together in front of the paddock like a blanket of wispy clouds. Papa lifts the barrier to the sheepfold and counts all the sheep as they go through to the other side of the fence one by one. I come down from my little mound and mingle with the animals. As they go by, I can't stop myself from touching their downy wool, which feels like cotton candy without the stickiness. They're so soft. You could almost mistake them for any other sheep when they're frolicking on the Screed.

But their wool is so light and airy that when you throw it, it's even slower to fall than a feather. And when there's a wind blowing, it flies away like a helium balloon. Apparently, they use it for insulation in jackets and partitions. Usually, the Woollybacks would be sheared tomorrow. But we're leaving soon on a big trip, and we need to pen them up before returning them to the menagerie. And that could be tricky, because they've never gotten used to living inside… A hoof thumps the ground next to me, and I smile. Good thing we have an ally to keep them all in check…

NAME: Aerolith
FLAVOR_TEXT: With Aerolith, gravity no longer constrains how we build.
STORY:
393 AC - My days as a lapidary are long behind me, yet there’s something soothing about the relationship a stonecutter has with a piece of rock. I study its texture, its transparency, its crevices — and all its flaws. It’s a difficult material to shape — far less so than the pebbles found near the Mirror, granted, but still. Nothing can chip those stones. Even so, focus is essential. If the Aerolith begins to resonate, it will reveal its exothermic properties, and that could prove dangerous — both for me and for the vessel I’ve made my home. To polish and facet these crystals, you need specialized equipment capable of absorbing residual energy. And even then, the process remains risky…

Be that as it may, the airships of the armada rely on these new supplies — and what better way to pass the time than by devoting myself to such work? These are welcome pauses before plunging back into the turbulence of guild assemblies. I set the mineral down on its stand, and my eyes drift to the letter lying across my workbench. I pick it up and examine it, studying the seals of the Ordis and the Tagmata. It seems to be from Zhen. I smile. Of course I remembered her — her parents’ estate, our studies, our long conversations on the patio… I was young then, with my whole life ahead of me. How old was she — ten, maybe? That was before the founding of the Axiom. Before the debates and the politics…

NAME: Zhen & Zephyr
FLAVOR_TEXT: Those who stand without honor will fall without wings

NAME: The Ugly Duckling
FLAVOR_TEXT: This young recruit swans about while proudly showing off his insignia.
INSPIRATION: Hans Christian Andersen's famous tale The Ugly Duckling tells the story of a young duckling who, rejected by his family, wanders far and wide to escape the insults and mockery thrown at him. At the end of a long journey, during which he continues to be ridiculed by everyone he meets, he realizes he has grown – and isn't a duck after all. He is in fact a magnificent swan. This rite-of-passage story highlights the idea that we must accept who we are, despite the mockery of those around us, and that a difference can ultimately be an asset, and a sign of recognition.
STORY:
393 AC - Unable to concentrate, I close the book and set it on the table. "Nye Eventyr. Første bind." This collection of tales has always been on my nightstand for obvious and childish reasons. Rejected by everyone. Mocked. I'd always been considered the ugly duckling of my class and neighborhood. The question was whether I'd eventually become a swan, or if I'd always be the unloved offspring. I can't stop myself from chuckling. This is no time for moping. By now, the results of the elections must be known. If the spar in the City of Scholars had been working, the Gestalt would surely already be full of delighted cheers or cries of disappointment, depending on the result.

I pick up a pen and write a few words in a notebook. The Ugly Duckling answers my call and stares at me with its big eyes. I calmly pet its head. Yes, little guy, you and I are are a lot alike. But this chapter isn't about me. If fate is on our side, this one will be about my sister and her future husband… I pace up and down my cabin with the Ugly Duckling resting in the palm of my hand. And I realize that I'm happy to suffer the consequences if it works in Anuncia's favor. I smile pathetically. Maybe I'm not so selfish after all? The door suddenly opens, and she barges in, completely out of breath. In her hand is a paper herald, and her green eyes stare at me…

NAME: Ascended Trooper
FLAVOR_TEXT: After months of expeditions, Aedyt felt she had finally spread her wings.
STORY:
393 AC - We make our way through the heart of the valley, and I'm already sweaty after several hours of walking. High in the sky, the Raptors soar above us, ensuring that we're not taken by surprise by any threat. One of them lands on a rocky peak, and I immediately recognize her by her red hair. Aedyt. Like Osoyo, she was given the chance to join Zhen's unit, an honor that suits her perfectly. She has attracted lots of birds, which fly around her with curiosity, and she's also drawn the Rear Admiral's attention. Her large paper wings expand, helping her to remain stable at the top of the rocky edifice. When they're not keeping watch, the Tagmata troops stay busy with various tasks, including information gathering and topographical surveys.

We walk underneath the tree canopy. Here amidst their thorny branches, the darkness is overwhelming. From the corner of my eye, I suddenly see Aedyt straighten. Through the Gestalt, I inhale the scent of coffee while she shares her perceptions with me. I see the steaming cup, and the thermos that she's closed back up. And I see the huge water sphere heading to a mountainous promontory. Yes, she's right – if we wait too long, the bubble will burst, and torrents of water will flood into the valley, down to where we are. I give the order to Tocsin to sound his horn. The blast rings out through the valley, and clouds of birds take off into the sky. We'll need to be quick. Aedyt leaves her perch and hovers above us before rejoining her squadron.

NAME: Ordis Warden
FLAVOR_TEXT: You can't beat the clink for catching forty winks.
STORY:
393 AC - The man wedged comfortably in his chair is snoring. I walk slowly along the rows of prison cells to the office. Most of them are empty. Only two are occupied: one by a Bravos still pickling in a heady cloud of alcohol, and the other by an irritated recruit who must have tried to stand up to him. I walk past the isolation cell. Luckily for her, the offence wasn't serious enough for her to be placed in solitary confinement. I remembered a soldier who had received such a punishment once. It wasn't just the padded cell that was torture; it was the solitude. Complete and total isolation. Being cut off from the Gestalt, even temporarily, could be the worst punishment imaginable. It was like swimming on the surface of a deep, dark sea and feeling the emptiness beneath…

I stand up straight in front of the guard and clear my throat. He opens his eyes and looks at me, without a hint of guilt at being caught napping. He clicks his tongue against the roof of his mouth. Maybe he's waiting for me to beg for the release of the young cadet? He probably doesn't suspect that it's him I've come to see. According to my information, the man in front of me – how old is he, 40? 45? – was the personal assistant of General De Graaf before becoming a prison officer on the Mandjet. Obviously he was far too young to have been in that position at the time of the incident, but as a secretary, maybe he'd got wind of something interesting before he took office…

NAME: Bluecap
FLAVOR_TEXT: To avoid sudden jolts, invest in stone.
INSPIRATION: In English folklore, Bluecaps are mythical fairies or ghosts that inhabit mines. They usually appear as a small blue flame. They are said to help miners by guiding them to rich deposits or warning them of potential dangers – in exchange for fair payment, of course.
STORY:
393 AC - Clack. Clack clack. His fingers move nimbly over the abacus. The beads slide from one row to another, while the little fellow sitting on the desk makes emphatic sounds, sometimes of surprise, sometimes of contentment. Clack. Clack clack clack. I watch him without batting an eyelash, even as irritation is making my moustache bristle. But I stop myself from making any kind of remark. I'm well aware that he's not the cause of my irritation; rather, it's the thoughts constantly churning in my head. Staying in the background has its pros and cons. On the one hand, it allows me to keep an eye on Asgartha through the reports I receive. On the other hand, it gives me too much time to dwell on my own thoughts. Did I do the right thing? Will Kojo give the game away? When?

I look at the Aerolith stocks requested by the Bravos for their spears. And the Bluecap continues to count, calculate and annotate. I sigh because all I can do is wait for his verdict. I took this task on with a definite aim. I felt I needed some rest, and that painful sensation of having forgotten something had gradually lessened after a while. But it hadn't completely disappeared. There was also plenty of research to do on those Phoenixian Guards. Were they just the custodians of Rune's prophecy? Was that really all? There was a mystery to be solved there. Discreetly, of course, with Mack on the frontline. With a satisfied sigh, the Bluecap finally puts his abacus down. It seems the figures add up.

NAME: Melusine
FLAVOR_TEXT: Every broken promise demands retribution.
INSPIRATION: Melusine is a female freshwater spirit from European folklore, often found in a holy well or river. She is usually depicted as a half-woman, half-serpent (or fish in some depictions), and she is sometimes given wings, two tails, or both. Legends about her are often connected with the northern and western regions of France, Luxembourg and the Netherlands. A major theme in the tales about her involves keeping one's promises.
STORY:
393 AC - We pass between the liquid spheres, watching their movement closely. The gravity here is erratic, to say the least. The bubbles sometimes start to spin faster before colliding and melding together. But the Quadrant seems stable, for now. I signal to my Raptors to take the starboard current, while Zephyr and I go around the other side. It would be costly to be taken by surprise by a Leviathan hiding behind one of these bubbles. Zeph, are you rea… Something hits my wings with full force, and I spin around before tumbling like a stone. My blood runs cold when I see my paper wing stump steaming and drenched as though it had been out in the pouring rain.

It's been cut by a hot liquid, which continues to evaporate before my eyes. But there's no time to dwell on my shock. I conjure new sheets to make more origami feathers, and I finally manage to stabilize myself before touching the cloud surface. After dodging another lance of hissing, boiling water, I look up to see who attacked me, while my swan honks in outrage. The Eidolon of Melusine dances on the surface of a sphere. I guess I must have stirred up a hornet's nest by going to see De Graaf's assistant. Melusine has a habit of punishing those who get a little too nosy. And I can't deny the accusation…

NAME: Gargoyle
FLAVOR_TEXT: At the slightest sign of intrusion, these stone lookouts come to life and sound the alarm.
INSPIRATION: Gargoyles are grotesque and monstrous statues that look out from the roofs of European churches like sentinels. They also drain water running off the roofs of these religious buildings, spitting it out of their half-open mouths. They were considered by many to be guardians, and their role was to protect these sacred places and drive away evil, both demons and sinners.
STORY:
393 AC - The lookouts placed by the Chimaera are blue marble with white veins: gargoyles, sculpted all along the deck, constantly scanning the sky, just like she does. Like the Alter Ego of the Aegis captain, their movement is restricted to a bare minimum – just a head that sometimes turns to look out into the distance. Since the first attacks, security measures have been reinforced, as has the general state of alert. And I'm more vigilant too, maybe more so than necessary… Like these silent and virtually motionless sentinels, I'm on my guard. Over the last few days, I've rarely left the interior of the flagship, and when I do go out, I'm always escorted by my Raptors. There haven't been any more attempts on my life.

All I know is that Gulrang and Tocsin are unlikely to be the ones behind the attacks on me. They would have the ability to do it in terms of Alteration, but I can't imagine them betraying me. So who could it be? When I probed the subconscious of the prison guard, I must have set off an alarm. The strongbox had been emptied of all compromising memories, of course, but the architect of this mechanism had installed a discreet warning system. Had De Graaf been informed? Suddenly, one of the gargoyles raises its head and looks to the west. Zephyr takes flight. It's coming from the Pelagonian Quadrant. The Mandjet's sirens start to sound almost immediately, and I open myself to the Gestalt again. The call for help cries out across all channels. It's coming from a mining station. The AES Sune is the first to respond to the distress signal.

NAME: Ordis Messenger
FLAVOR_TEXT: To maintain their cohesion, the Ordis must call on the most reliable of couriers.
STORY:
393 AC - The recruits hurry to collect their rations. I walk past them. Many of them think the odyssey is a time for rest, but it's not a peaceful rest. The Leviathans prowling overhead and under the clouds are to blame for that. But what can you really do against such monsters? We're like ants trying to stand up to the shadow of a boot. Nina fills her bowl with great care, and Helder takes a big helping of stew. I scan the crowd, looking for Kojo, who must be in the line somewhere. I don't know what's bothering him, but he's been lost in his thoughts recently. He seems worried. He's not speaking much. And that's not like him. He's distracted as well… But that is like him.

As I look around the sea of faces, I notice Osoyo. He smiles at me and nods, and I do the same. Maybe that's his way of thanking me for coming to his rescue during his last descent into the Crow's Eye. Or maybe it's because I supported his candidacy for joining the Tagmata. The last I heard, he'd joined Zhen's Raptors. Yes, he'd had experience in working alongside an Exalt. But he was also just a good recruit, as I'd suspected from the start. He deserved all the credit, and the promotion was definitely justified. I leave him chatting with the rest of his squad, and I turn away. And I'm well aware that I'm smiling at the same time.

NAME: Doppelgänger
FLAVOR_TEXT: Such fluidity reflects countless possibilities.
INSPIRATION: In Germanic folklore, a Doppelgänger is a ghostly being, an evil double who whispers bad thoughts to its twin. It is often a bad omen that predicts misfortune or the death of the original person.
STORY:
393 AC - The spheres burst one after another, and some of them transform into dragons at Melusine's bidding. Zeph. I don't need to explain myself. My Chimaera detaches and dives to port, taking a few draconic creatures with him. But I still have a few on my back, along with the fairy's Eidolon… I need to shake them off. Who had summoned her? I'd learned something interesting by delving into the prison guard's mind. More than a mere assistant, the man had actually been a strongbox, trained to filter, encrypt and protect crucial, secret or even illegal information from any curious person within the Gestalt. Given the ambush targeting me, I had obviously got too close for someone's comfort.

I look back at the fairy chasing me. I fly really close to a water bubble, using its roundness to hide me a tiny bit. It's just enough for me to use Heka without her noticing. Under the water, I summon a Doppelgänger and tell it to follow me. Little by little, its abstract features become more defined and begin to resemble my own. It's a watery copy, which I then modify using Alteration to give it color and body… When I'm ready, I accelerate for two or three seconds, then order my lookalike to shoot out of the water while I dive. I hold my breath as I watch Melusine pursue my twin. I've shaken her off for now, but I need to know who summoned her.

NAME: Sagitta, Soaring Leviathan
FLAVOR_TEXT: We flew higher to escape the turbulence of its wings.
STORY:
393 AC - I step out on deck as the sirens blare all around us. Soldiers and recruits rush to their stations, but many of them pause, open-mouthed, when they see the size of the Leviathan in front of us. And I can understand why… It's obviously a bird, a bird of prey, but its size… It could easily grab one of our transporters in its talons. I receive a string of information through the Gestalt: "Sagittarius serpentarius", "Secretarybird", "Sagittariidae family"… I contact my own Raptors, and all of them reply with their "Supero!" to indicate they are ready. All of them are converging on the drop zone. I feel a gust of wind on my face as Zephyr lands near me.

For now, the Leviathan seems content to watch the transporters as they fight against the turbulence of its gigantic wings. Its instinctual curiosity is strong. But that curiosity could quickly become more tactile, especially if it becomes angry or playful. We may have reacted promptly, but we can't handle an adversary like this. All we can do is keep its attention and distract it from the other ships. I think of the various possible tactics and the different approach vectors. For now, senior command is adamant that we hold off on launching a barrage, but if that does become necessary, our operation will become even more difficult… I turn to my squad, which is now fully assembled. I don't need to give a speech. The task speaks for itself, and the stakes are obvious and clear. We don't have any other choice. Supero.

NAME: Yanna, Qorgan Agent
FLAVOR_TEXT: Spies from the Qorgan infiltrate the Factions and steal their secrets.
STORY:
393 AC - It's an instinct you develop when you learn to read body language and all those non-verbal signals that people send out, sometimes against their will… Fear, aversion, interest and many other clues that reveal our thoughts, even if we try to hide them. The Rear Admiral is successfully hiding many of these concealed messages under her stoicism and the reserve that goes with her rank. But it's not enough to fool a trained eye. She's sniffing around. She's looking for something, and trying to hide it from her peers and superiors. It's a jarring combination. She knows her actions are illicit. Her tense muscles give it away. But at the same time, her determination indicates that she's doing it with a sense of justice. She wants to dig something up, but bury it at the same time.

I don't think she's a threat. As a matter of fact, I think I could use her. Ever since she visited the prison, she's been targeted. Twice, even. She survived the first attempt on her own. The second time, I had to use a mind impulse to make the butler trip, ensuring that the poisoned drink fell to the ground before he could serve it to her. What hornet's nest has she disturbed? Now I need to choose my strategy. Should I keep my distance and simply watch? Should I take a look into her mind, at the risk of leaving evidence of my foray? I could also try to make her an ally. I close my eyes and reach out to Suha. What would you do, my love?

NAME: Nike
FLAVOR_TEXT: When she spreads her wings, her victory shall resonate for all eternity.
INSPIRATION: In Greek mythology, Nike is the goddess of victory and triumph. She is the daughter of the Titan Pallas and the Oceanid Styx. Her brothers are Zelus, Bia and Kratos, who represent zeal, force and power respectively.
STORY:
393 AC - We approach in close formation, making good use of the updrafts. I keep an eye on my squad, especially the new recruits who only joined the Tagmata recently. They're in position, despite the youngest one's somewhat shaky command of her wings. But she'll arrive safely. We use the thick cloud cover as much as we can to avoid attracting the Leviathan's attention. And the closer we are, the more the monster's massive size becomes apparent. Its dark eye is fixed on the transport barge, and its beak pecks at the liquid sphere the ship is dragging behind it. I clench my teeth. We'll need to act quickly. Zephyr and half of my marines fly off towards the other ships so they can steer them away from the monster. And as for us…

I swoop towards the Leviathan's head, followed by the rest of my intervention squad. I retract my wings to go into freefall… Desperate times call for desperate measures. I trace the Heka signs, and she leaps out of the verses I write for her – Nike and her wings of victory. Like a comet, she rips through the clouds, and we follow as she enters the Serpent-Eagle-Leviathan's field of vision. The monster is suddenly much more interested in our procession rather than the ship, especially now that the goddess has lit her flame and is shining brilliantly, like the tip of an arrow sparkling in the sun. The Leviathan beats its wings to chase after us. We've done it – we've grabbed its attention.

NAME: Out of a Clear Sky
FLAVOR_TEXT: A swarm of messages bursts forth in a rustling of paper.
STORY:
393 AC - "Paper heralds incoming." The Gestalt had suddenly lit up as reports started to spread through all the communication channels. Zhen's Raptors have spotted a murmuration of messages coming from Asgartha. According to their estimates, there are hundreds. It seems I'm not the only one who asked for news. No real surprise there. I clench my fist, both nervous and impatient to find out the results of the votes. Some of these messages will reach the admiralty, and Singh will soon be opening her missive and discovering her fate. And the fate awaiting all of us. Will the Expeditionary Corps be ordered to turn back? Or will reinforcements be sent, including more Exalts?

I start to think about those who stayed in Asgartha, either because they weren't ready or because they were given other missions… I also start to think of Shan-shu, whose exploits were a part of my childhood. Seeing his swan had been a shock. I was aware he'd survived, of course, despite splitting from his Alterer. But seeing him fly again with Zhen had revived memories from long ago. What had become of those first Exalts, of those who came before us, even before that name had been officially announced? Something taps at the window, and I stand up. I see an origami chicken on the window ledge… It's time to read the verdict.

NAME: Ordis Signet
FLAVOR_TEXT: Cohesion and justice.
STORY:
393 AC - "United in the throng. This is the ultimate meaning of the Gestalt. It is the fruit of a harmonious, shared, immediate and permanent collaboration. Coalescence is the surrendering of individuality in favor of a coming together of multiple spirits. United, bare in thought. United, bare in emotion. United, staunch in fellowship. United, staunch in our virtues. The Gestalt breaks down distance, borders, physical obstacles and the limitations of the self. The Rhombus that marks our flesh is proof of our commitment, proof that we offer up our individuality to the greater good of the community. There is no stronger vow. Our affiliation is one of total devotion and self-sacrifice. When others become part of yourself, the idea of justice is obvious. When others become part of yourself, we can move mountains."

I listen to the officiant as he faces the… congregation. I feel their communion in the melting pot of their shared mind, as their thoughts begin to resonate. There are a few soldiers, clerics, politicians, scribes, scholars and many other identities among them. I move through them like an undetectable wave. I can't help thinking of the entity of the City of Scholars, the one that ultimately strived for a union similar to the Gestalt. It was the city, and it wanted everyone to live in harmony. In it. Within it. I don't think anyone perceived that side of it. Its appetite wasn't driven by an instinct for destruction – quite the opposite, in fact. It was driven by a desire for unity, however flawed that desire was.

NAME: Soar
FLAVOR_TEXT: A Zephyr feather gives the Ordis the ability to fly.
STORY:
393 AC - The chimeric swan slowly unfolds its azure wing, and the Rear Admiral plucks a few feathers to give to us. I take one, glancing at the Leviathan, which almost fills the whole sky. Its shrieks rend the air, and I have to stop myself from covering my ears with trembling hands. A reassuring hum breaks the surface of my consciousness. It's Osoyo, urging me to stay calm with a caress of his mind. I glance at him before attaching the feather to the strap of my breastplate. I try to clear my mind, to pull out the ideas contained within the feather and translate them into signs, letters and words. I conjure sheets of paper on which the Glyphs are then progressively inscribed.

The letters become words, the words become sentences, then lines, then paragraphs, spreading from sheet to sheet. I know I need to focus more than the others, but the process is taking less and less effort. Little by little, the paper wings that unfold on my back are becoming more natural, like extensions of my own body. I flap them to test their weight and lift. It hadn't been easy at first, but with practice, I had gotten the hang of it. I approach the edge and see the clouds floating beneath us. Falling down there would be certain death… I take a deep breath. It's not always a good idea to think too much about these things. It's my turn, so I let myself fall. And then I unfurl my wings.

NAME: Skybound Odyssey
FLAVOR_TEXT: Like a beacon, the horizon calls us onward!
STORY:
393 AC - The pillar of light. Over there, pinned to the horizon like a tower that goes up forever, beyond this new atoll and much bigger than the others we've encountered. It's lit up like a beacon, visible in almost every situation. Thankfully, even though there have been a few hazards, the journey has been easier than expected. The water spheres provide us with drinking water, and the archipelagos have all the nourishment we need so we don't have to dip into our food stocks… And as for morale, the floating islands break up the monotony of the sea of clouds and allow us to take some beneficial breaks on their surfaces. Even so, this blazing column is a haunting presence. It's always there in our peripheral vision, except when the high clouds occasionally hide it. And at night, it almost conceals the light of certain stars…

Who turned on this signal? Why? What will we find when we get there? There are so many questions, and I imagine every member of the Expeditionary Corps is eager for answers, not just me. But our odyssey keeps moving forward at a steady pace. Zephyr trumpets, and I start to slalom between the watery bubbles. Yes, we have a mission. Danger is constantly lurking. I signal to my Raptors, and we change formation to cover more ground. The Mandjet, which is following behind us, needs its scouts. It needs our full concentration. I'll have plenty of time to continue my investigations once we get back home.

NAME: Mandjet
FLAVOR_TEXT: Mandjet and Mesektet, the Ordis flagships, reunited at last.
STORY:
393 AC - Thirty-five years. They had waited all this time before starting repairs on the Day Barque. Although the Mesektet had been lost for good, the same couldn't be said about the Mandjet. Yes, the flagship had suffered severe damage, but it was far from being a complete wreck. It was the pride of the Aegis, having reigned supreme over the sky of Asgartha. It was a symbol of protection for its citizens. So why leave it to gather dust for multiple decades in a shipyard warehouse in Sadracca? Repairs hadn't officially started until 375 AC. When you really thought about it, there was something suspicious about that. Of course, you could argue that a lack of materials had prevented the work from being started… but at the expense of risking the sky and the security of the Protectorate?

No, something wasn't right. Gaj was now in charge of the Mandjet. I had an equivalent rank, but it was mainly given to me as an honorary title because I was part of an Exalt. Unlike other ships in the Asgarthan fleet, there were many areas on the Mandjet that my authorization level didn't allow me to access. Even though I was a Rear Admiral. I've heard that some spies can use the Gestalt to implant their consciousness within another's while remaining undetectable. I don't know if it's true or just an urban legend, but I could certainly do with having such an ability in my current situation…

NAME: The Origamium
FLAVOR_TEXT: Where paper heralds take flight.
STORY:
393 AC - I wait impatiently for the election results. The paper heralds must be flitting around the Origamium by now. Dragonflies, grasshoppers, doves and crows… The origamophiles must be sorting them and releasing them towards their final destination. And one of those folded pieces of paper is on its way to me, bearing the name of the person who will succeed Avkan. There must be hundreds or even thousands of them, swirling around in a rustling of crumpled paper. I look out the window, fully aware that I won't receive a missive today… In the meantime, I decide to do my mental exercises. It's become a routine recently. I can't afford to let my mind fail again…

Thinking is all I know how to do. The Rati doctors believe I suffered the same illness as the other labyrinth explorers. But why did the symptoms start well before we arrived at the City of Scholars? I can almost hear the rustling of paper wings… Unless that's just the whir of my thoughts constantly turning over in my head. But I haven't suffered any other symptoms, and I haven't had any irrefutable proof of actual degeneration. "You're worrying about nothing, old man." Mack is snooping around the ventilation ducts in the Ouroboros, looking for information. He's probably right. Fear is the enemy of the mind, and I need to banish it…

NAME: Mana Moth
FLAVOR_TEXT: A rain of Mana, a source of magic.
STORY:
393 AC - I have to act fast. I thread the chimeran silk into the automated spool and engage the rewinding mechanism. Better to use the Alter Ego’s threads than my own. Silk’s filament wraps around my needle, which I hold like a rapier. Before me, above the rippling waters, a monstrous moth has taken form, its mandibles snapping shut. It has never known hunger before, and thus cannot understand what it feels now. I glance at the Exalt—they have already begun to act. I need to synchronize with them to banish this abomination. I lunge, piercing one of its wings, then anchor a thread into the ground to prevent it from taking flight.

The Alterer plunges his hand into the Empyrean, seeking to grasp the very concept of evaporation. He intends to dissipate the water, purify the idea, and return it to its original state. No—there’s no time for that. I draw my pins from their sheath and fling them at the mutated insect. Not that I want to start an entomological collection, but better to ensure the Muna, frozen a few steps away, doesn’t become an impromptu snack. My needles pin it to the rocky wall. Silk swivels toward me, exuding reproach. Nearby, I feel Sam’s presence, ready to intervene. Her eyes glint in the night, but I signal that I’ve got the situation under control.

NAME: Moyo & Silk
FLAVOR_TEXT: The idea of the butterfly resides within the caterpillar

NAME: Undine
FLAVOR_TEXT: When Yzmir alchemists call on the water spirit, the mischievous undine responds.
INSPIRATION: Undines are creatures from Germanic folklore, depicted as water spirits much like nymphs and naiads. They are found in running water, rivers and fountains. Some of them guard treasure in underwater areas. It's said that they supply water to fountains, and dry them up if they feel offended.
